Read this before trusting the numbers

All three scenarios return identical results. The engine recorded zero direction conflicts across the whole period, so Block, Queue and Hedge never actually diverge. With a $1.111 stop, trades close long before the histogram can flip colour — median hold is 0 bars. These three options only differ if trades survive long enough to see a flip.

The stop is smaller than the bars. Median M15 range in this data is $8.86, about 8x the $1.111 stop. Whether a trade wins or loses is therefore decided by the path inside a candle, which 15-minute OHLC cannot tell us. I assume the adverse extreme comes first (the conservative reading); assuming otherwise flips the result from roughly +$3,000 to +$20,000. Treat the absolute figures as indicative only.

Entries are the revised rules you specified: primary fires on body-break OR X-Trend-clear, amber no longer closes trades, and positions exit only on their own trailing stop.
